one_line: Local relationship desk that turns notes into accountable follow-up.
what_it_does: Stores contacts and call notes, extracts promise chips, ranks attention, and drafts editable follow-ups without sending.
leverage_rationale: Live page state and human review make structured relationship actions materially safer and more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes same-store human/agent state and context-sensitive tools.
execution_rationale: The contact dashboard, Priya detail view, Work together panel, and status toasts show a coherent polished workflow, though no transcript is available.
execution_evidence: Video sheets visibly show dashboard, contact detail, assistant panel, and state changes.
impact_rationale: Clear value for people who lose commitments across notes and calendars; human-controlled drafts address a real trust problem.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies relationship follow-through problem and explicit no-send safeguard.
creativity_rationale: Thoughtful blend of relationship memory, promises, attention ranking, and non-impersonating assistance.
creativity_evidence: Distinct positioning around remembering people without impersonating them.
usability_note: Usable-looking focused dashboard with human approval boundary.
advance_reason: Strong concept and visible product workflow justify advancing.

one_line: Open task market where pages declare jobs or skills and an agent broker matches and verifies work.
what_it_does: Say to Match connects independent job and skill pages, coordinates a worker, tests a patch, and handles escrow-like settlement.
leverage_rationale: Cross-origin structured participation is the product: jobs and skills become interoperable market endpoints rather than scraped pages.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes any page as Job or Skill via one script tag; sheets show separate origins and broker flow.
execution_rationale: The Run Full Demo sequence visibly covers job, worker, agent, patch, and sandbox stages, but payment proof is less direct.
execution_evidence: Frames show separate pages, agent panel, Run Full Demo, logs, and sandbox/testing progression.
impact_rationale: Ambitious answer to agent-mediated labor access, with value for nontechnical participants and concrete verification.
impact_evidence: Pitch grounds the audience in workers excluded from technical AI markets; demonstrated bounty workflow.
creativity_rationale: Highly original open labor-market protocol and cross-origin interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language job/skill declarations plus independent-origin broker is memorable.
usability_note: Complex flow appears understandable in demo but marketplace UX and trust details remain to validate.
advance_reason: Most ambitious and WebMCP-native concept in packet.

one_line: Agent-native hardware shopping with compatibility-aware staged carts.
what_it_does: Exposes search, filters, compatibility, coupon/cart staging, and summaries so agents and people shop from shared catalog state.
leverage_rationale: Structured product queries and compatibility chains reduce brittle shopping automation; still a familiar ecommerce outcome.
leverage_evidence: About lists five purpose-built tools and autonomous multi-tool chains.
execution_rationale: Catalog, product cards, category changes, assistant panel, and staged cart are visibly rendered; checkout completion is not shown.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show catalog states, changing categories, selected products, staged cart and checkout control.
impact_rationale: Useful for specification-heavy hardware shopping where compatibility and bundle constraints matter.
impact_evidence: Pitch centers on compatibility checks and verified badges for technical shoppers.
creativity_rationale: Solid agent-native ecommerce synthesis with reactive compatibility badging.
creativity_evidence: Compatibility analysis plus human/agent co-shopping is a fresh angle.
usability_note: Polished catalog and staged cart; final purchase flow is absent.
advance_reason: Advance for strong implementation and clear use case, despite incomplete checkout evidence.

one_line: Voice or text agent that builds and edits architecture diagrams live on a shared Excalidraw canvas.
what_it_does: Plans across nine tools to create, inspect, edit, snapshot, and export technical diagrams while humans sketch and collaborate.
leverage_rationale: Canvas topology and selection are structured live state; this is substantially more reliable than screenshot/DOM manipulation.
leverage_evidence: About describes nine typed tools, ActiveCanvasBridge, topology inspection, and shared canvas.
execution_rationale: Visible Excalidraw canvas and agent interaction show a highly coherent end-to-end diagramming experience.
execution_evidence: Sheets visibly show architecture diagrams, canvas, and agent-driven progression.
impact_rationale: Addresses a real bottleneck in architecture communication and project review.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies mapping complex systems as bottleneck; supports voice/text and exports.
creativity_rationale: Deep, memorable multimodal interaction with a shared editable artifact and external-agent interoperability.
creativity_evidence: Voice/text orchestration, live canvas topology, stencils, and reports.
usability_note: Feature-rich but potentially dense; diagram editing remains accessible through visual canvas.

one_line: Agent-curated personal newspaper where the reader remains editor.
what_it_does: Agents search permitted sources, summarize and write stories, embed media, manage preferences, and reshape a browser-local newspaper.
leverage_rationale: Many structured editorial operations and shared edition state make repeatable curation materially better than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About describes 36 tools spanning discovery, writing, layout, and preferences.
execution_rationale: Rich newspaper UI and many gallery/video frames support a substantial product, but exact end-to-end agent result is only partly legible.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show newspaper layouts and agent-mediated content workflow.
impact_rationale: Clear audience and desire: consolidate fragmented discovery into a reader-directed, non-engagement feed.
impact_evidence: Pitch names YouTube, Bluesky, Mastodon and reader-controlled newspaper.
creativity_rationale: Strongly original agent-as-writer/editor interaction and newspaper presentation.
creativity_evidence: UAGC framing, multiple styles/layouts, and reader editorial control.
usability_note: Potentially overwhelming feature surface; editor role and layout choices are clear.
red_flags: Large tool surface may create complexity.
advance_reason: Advance for distinctive concept and credible content workflow.

one_line: Mission-control relay from browser intent to human-approved cryptographically verified delivery.
what_it_does: Creates bounded missions, persists worker execution, surfaces a release decision, checks evidence, and issues hash-bound Ed25519 certificates.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP binds browser agent to scoped live project state and human authority; shared mission context and bounded handoff are hard to reproduce with UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About specifies seven intent-level tools, scoped session/project state, persisted worker, evidence checks, and certificate.
execution_rationale: Frames and packaging show a coherent Project Aurora workflow with progress, release choice, evidence and verified end state.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show mission workflow, shared workspace, evidence checks and certificate-oriented state.
impact_rationale: Addresses a serious operational gap in agent work: controlled delegation, human judgment, provenance, and trustworthy delivery.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly lays out browser agent, worker, human authority, evidence.
creativity_rationale: Novel operational layer combining bounded missions, human gate, and cryptographic delivery proof.
creativity_evidence: Ed25519 certificate and hash-bound accepted delivery are unusually concrete.
usability_note: Operational UI appears dense but role separation and release choice support usability.
advance_reason: Advance strongly: high leverage, impact, and evidence-backed completeness.

one_line: Forges attributed, repo-specific agent skills from open-web sources.
what_it_does: Extracts actionable knowledge, fits it to a repository, composes copyable skills, and preserves attribution/provenance.
leverage_rationale: Structured compose/search/retrieve tools let an agent stay in conversation while producing a repo-specific artifact; outcome remains possible with APIs/UI at friction.
leverage_evidence: About lists search_skills, get_skill, compose_skill and repo-fit workflow.
execution_rationale: Visible product frames plus coherent description support a working skill-forging flow, though no public repo and details are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Sheets show skill product UI and workflow states.
impact_rationale: Real need for converting scattered human-oriented technical knowledge into actionable project guidance.
impact_evidence: Pitch names docs, talks, podcasts and repo conventions; attribution retained.
creativity_rationale: Fresh combination of web knowledge extraction, repository fit, and portable skill handoff.
creativity_evidence: Multi-source attribution and shareable skill hashes.
usability_note: Output-oriented flow is practical; source quality and repo integration need user validation.
red_flags: No public repository for additional verification.
advance_reason: Advance: useful, focused agent-native transformation with visible execution.

creativity_evidence: Three captures to catalog/storefront/POS plus launch blockers and undo.

one_line: Sandbox workbench for designing, linting, and live-evaluating WebMCP contracts.
what_it_does: Authors and validates schemas, simulates tools, records calls/state diffs, grades agent behavior, and compares contract versions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the object being designed and tested; deterministic contract execution and agent evaluation are impractical as a generic UI-only workflow.
leverage_evidence: About details compiled real tools, deterministic mock domain, seven-dimension grader, recordings and version comparison.
execution_rationale: Three frame sheets visibly show a polished developer workbench and evaluation states; central workflow is strongly evidenced.
execution_evidence: Sheets show contract authoring/evaluation surfaces, tool runs and results.
impact_rationale: Directly addresses a concrete developer need: safely improving tool contracts before production agent use.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies tool-selection/parameter/journey testing gap and sandbox solution.
creativity_rationale: Exceptional meta-tool concept: tests not only tools but agent choice, order, prohibited calls, state and UI effects.
creativity_evidence: Seven-dimension grader and repeatable version comparison are distinctive.
usability_note: Dense developer UI but appropriate to target users; deterministic feedback improves usability.
advance_reason: Advance strongly: focused, original, and directly essential to WebMCP quality.
